title: I like music
goal: Talk about hobbies and likes, and fit in the dative pronouns *îmi, îți, îi, ne, vă, le* — because in Romanian you don't "like" something; it "pleases you".
bekal: say what you like and dislike with *îmi place / îmi plac* and *nu-mi place*
choose *place* or *plac* according to the thing liked, and give it the definite article
stress who likes it with *mie, ție, lui, ei, nouă, vouă, lor* and with names: *Lui Andrei îi place…*

notes: **Îmi place muzica = "music pleases me".** The verb *a plăcea* works the other way round from "like": the thing liked is the **subject**, and the person who likes it only appears as the little word *îmi* ("to me"). That's why the verb agrees with the thing liked, not with the person — like Spanish *me gusta*.

**Ascult muzică, but îmi place muzica.** As an ordinary object, *muzică* can be bare. But as the subject of *place*, something liked in general **must take the definite article**: *muzica, filmele, fotbalul, marea*.

**Nu-mi place.** *Nu* + *îmi* merge into *nu-mi*. The same goes for *nu-ți* and *nu-i*; the other three don't merge: *nu ne, nu vă, nu le*. The word *deloc* (at all) stands at the end and is only used with *nu*.

**Și mie îmi place.** *Mie* is the stressed form of *îmi*, used when the person is highlighted: "**me** too". Notice that *îmi* is still there — the stressed form never replaces the short form, it only keeps it company.

**Munte → muntele → munții.** The singular with article uses *-le* because it ends in *-e* (unit 4); the plural with article is *munții*, with two *i*s (unit 6). *La munte* has no article, following the golden rule of prepositions.

grammars.title: Dative pronouns and place versus plac
body: The dative answers the question "to whom?". Each person has a short form that stands right in front of the verb, and a stressed form that can be added before it.
The verb itself has only two forms you need: **place** if the thing liked is singular, **plac** if it's plural.
after: **Place or plac is decided by the thing, not the person.** *Îmi place filmul* (one film) versus *Îmi plac filmele* (films in general). *Le place muzica* = "they like music": the people are plural, but *muzica* is singular, so *place*.
**The order is flexible.** The thing liked can come first: *Muzica românească îmi place foarte mult.* Only the short pronoun can't move — it always sticks to the front of the verb.
**Liking to do something** = *îmi place să* + verb: *Îmi place să citesc* (I like reading). The *să* form comes in unit 11; for now, learn it whole, and notice that here it's always *place*.

grammars.title: Negative and stressed forms
body: Two things make sentences about likes and dislikes come alive: merging with *nu*, and the stressed forms for comparing people's tastes.
after: **When is the stressed form used?** To contrast (*Mie îmi place ceaiul, dar ție îți place cafeaua*), and for short answers without a verb: *Și mie* (me too), *Mie nu* (not me), *Nici mie* (me neither).

**With people's names**, use *lui* + name, and the short pronoun is still required: *Lui Andrei îi place muntele. Lui Budi nu-i place fotbalul.* The sentence *Lui Andrei place muntele* is wrong — *îi* can't be left out. Female names ending in *-a* take a different ending (*Ioanei îi place marea*); that ending comes in unit 13, so for now just recognize it.

blocks.text: Watch out for twins: *mare* means "big" (adjective, unit 9) and also "sea" (feminine noun). Context always helps: *marea* with the article is definitely the sea, and *Marea Neagră* is the Black Sea, with beaches at Constanța and Mamaia.

blocks.title: Music and mountains
items: **Muzică populară** is folk music, still alive at parties and weddings, often accompanying the *hora* — a circle dance holding hands. From the classical world, the biggest name is the composer George Enescu; the festival named after him is held in București every two years.
**Weekends in the mountains** are a București habit. Sinaia, Bușteni, and Predeal in Valea Prahovei (the Prahova Valley) are about two hours away by train.

sections.title: How much do you like it?

blocks.text: *Ador*, *prefer*, and *detest* are ordinary *-a* group verbs (*a adora, a prefera, a detesta*): you are the subject, with no dative pronoun — just like English *love, prefer, hate*. But something spoken of in general still takes the definite article: *Ador marea. Prefer ceaiul.* And *nu prea* is a gentle way of saying you don't like something without offending your host.

head: Asking about tastes
English
rows: What do you do in your free time?
What kind of films do you like?
And you? — Me too. / Not me.

blocks.title: One small trap
items: *A plăcea* can also be used about people, and then the meaning shifts: *Îmi placi* ("you please me") usually sounds like "I fancy you". For friends, it's safer to say *Ești simpatic* (m) or *Ești simpatică* (f) — "you're nice".
